newsitem.title: USA: Army awards Taiwan missile contract.
newsitem.headline: Army awards Taiwan missile contract.

text.p: The Army announced a $63 million contract for Taiwan missiles on Monday, just days before a relations-mending trip to Washington by a China delegation headed by Chinese Defense Minister Chi Haotian.
The Defense Department approved the Taiwan sale last summer despite a warning from China's foreign ministry that it would cause "new damage" to improving U.S.-China relations.
Gen. Chi and a 20-member senior delegation from China's defense and foreign ministries is to arrive on Thursday for a two-week visit at the invitation of Defense Secretary William Perry.

The Army announced without elaboration that it had awarded the $63 million contract to Boeing Defense and Space Group, Missiles and Space Division in Huntsville, Alabama, to produce 74 Avenger fire units for Taiwan.
The Avenger is a mobile anti-aircraft defense missile system that can launch eight Stinger missiles from two reloadable pods.
